summary: No state-specific trans-related source was found for this division in the current research pass: no local incident series and no documented enforcement divergence from the national frame. The national law applies here in full — the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (up to 14 years, extends to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression of identity) plus the inherited criminal provisions; national monitoring recorded 89 extortions, 118 harassment incidents and more than 20 unlawful detentions of LGBTQ+ people by law-enforcement officials in 2024 alone, with detentions for "looking gay" and release on payment of a bribe reported. This division sits outside the twelve northern states that carry a separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct. Dating-app "kito" extortion gangs are a nationwide app-user risk, and foreign government travel advice warns LGBT travellers of arrest, violence and blackmail.

sources.summary: BBC News report (9 August 2024): police investigate the killing of a 33-year-old trans TikToker and sex worker known as "Abuja Area Mama", whose beaten body was found on a highway in the federal capital; she had reported a stabbing in September 2023 and had said she feared for her life; police described the victim as "a man fully dressed in female clothing with no means of identification"; the police chief ordered a "thorough and discreet" investigation.

Long-form report (February 2025) on the same killing: six months on, no suspects charged; the police classified it a "culpable homicide" and misgendered the body; nearly 6,000 signatures on a petition asking for hate-crime categorisation, met with misgendering abuse online; context on the 2014 Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act (up to 14 years; bans marriages, organisations and public promotion; colonial-era "carnal knowledge" laws remain), the death-by-stoning regime under Sharia in northern states, no legal gender change, and hormone therapy obtained through online international pharmacies without medical guidance.

Report (August 2026) on the latest UK travel advice for this country: warns LGBT+ travellers of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation; up to 14 years for same-sex sexual activity; some northern states' religious law can prescribe the death penalty; the 2014 Act also punishes assisting, attending or promoting same-sex relationships and LGBTQ+ organisations; separately warns of short-notice curfews and vehicle-movement restrictions, mobile-network shutdowns with little notice, and political rallies and communal violence.

outOfScopeNotes: Armed insurgency in the north-east (Boko Haram), kidnapping, and violent crime affect travellers in many parts of the country; these are general hazards, not trans-specific.
tangentialFactors: The 2014 Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act (up to 14 years, applies to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression) shapes police and prosecutorial posture toward anyone perceived as same-sex-active, including gender-nonconforming visitors, everywhere in this country including this division; dating-app "kito" extortion gangs present a documented app-user risk to gay and trans people alike. The separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct applies only in the twelve northern states, not in this division.
